supports.excerpt:
GRPO at scale: train a 70B+ Model on multiple nodes
When training large models like Qwen2.5-72B, you need several key optimizations to make the training efficient and scalable across multiple GPUs and nodes. These include:

- DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3: ZeRO leverages data parallelism to distribute model states (weights, gradients, optimizer states) across multiple GPUs and CPUs, reducing memory and compute requirements on each device. Since large models cannot fit on a single GPU, using ZeRO Stage 3 is required for training such model. For more details, see DeepSpeed Integration. 
- Accelerate: Accelerate is a library that simplifies distributed training across multiple GPUs and nodes. It provides a simple API to launch distributed training and handles the complexities of distributed training, such as data parallelism, gradient accumulation, and distributed data loading. For more details, see Distributing Training. 
- vLLM: See the previous section on how to use vLLM to speed up generation.

Below is an example SLURM script to train a 70B model with GRPO on multiple nodes. This script trains a model on 4 nodes and uses the 5th node for vLLM-powered generation.

skill_drafts.description: Configure and deploy DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3 to distribute model weights, gradients, and optimizer states across multiple GPUs and nodes, enabling training of 70B+ parameter models that cannot fit on a single device.
skill_drafts.objective: Enable memory-efficient distributed training of large language models
applicable_signals: Model parameter count exceeds single-GPU memory capacity
Training across multiple GPUs or nodes required
Memory footprint optimization needed for large parameter models
Out-of-memory errors encountered on single device
contraindications: Training small models that fit on a single GPU
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Install and configure DeepSpeed with ZeRO Stage 3 support', 'detail': 'Ensure DeepSpeed is installed and ZeRO Stage 3 is enabled in training configuration'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Define model state distribution strategy', 'detail': 'Configure ZeRO to partition weights, gradients, and optimizer states across available GPUs and CPUs'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Set up data parallelism across nodes', 'detail': 'Use Accelerate or equivalent to handle distributed data loading and gradient synchronization'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Launch distributed training job', 'detail': 'Submit training job via SLURM or cluster scheduler; verify all nodes and GPUs are active'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Monitor training and memory distribution', 'detail': 'Verify model states are distributed across devices and no out-of-memory errors occur'}
triggers: Training models larger than single-GPU memory capacity; scaling across multiple GPUs or nodes; optimizing memory footprint for large parameter counts
constraints: Requires multiple GPUs or nodes available
DeepSpeed library must be installed and configured
Distributed training framework (e.g., Accelerate) recommended for simplified orchestration
SLURM or equivalent job scheduler for multi-node deployment
cautions: ZeRO Stage 3 introduces communication overhead; verify network bandwidth between nodes
Gradient accumulation and data parallelism configuration must align with available hardware
Monitor per-device memory usage to ensure balanced distribution
output_contract: DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3 configuration successfully applied; model states distributed across devices; training initiated without out-of-memory errors; distributed training loop running across all allocated GPUs and nodes.

skill_drafts.name: Multi-Node Training Orchestration with Accelerate
skill_drafts.description: Use Accelerate library to simplify distributed training launch and management across multiple GPUs and nodes, handling data parallelism, gradient accumulation, and distributed data loading automatically.
skill_drafts.objective: Simplify and standardize multi-node training orchestration
applicable_signals: Training script ready for distributed execution
contraindications: Direct NCCL or torch.distributed API required
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Install and configure Accelerate', 'detail': 'Install Accelerate library; run accelerate config to detect and configure hardware setup (GPUs, nodes, parallelism strategy)'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Prepare training script', 'detail': 'Ensure training script is compatible with Accelerate; wrap model and data loading with Accelerate API calls'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Launch distributed training', 'detail': 'Use accelerate launch command to start training across all configured nodes; Accelerate handles device assignment and synchronization'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Monitor training execution', 'detail': 'Verify data parallelism and gradient accumulation are active; check logs for synchronization issues across nodes'}
triggers: Training launch across multiple nodes required
Distributed data loading must be managed
constraints: Accelerate must be installed and compatible with training framework
Hardware configuration must be accessible to Accelerate
Training script must be compatible with Accelerate launcher
Network connectivity between nodes must be stable
cautions: Ensure all nodes have identical Python and dependency versions
Verify network bandwidth sufficient for gradient synchronization
Test configuration on subset of nodes before full-scale training
output_contract: Accelerate configuration created and validated; distributed training launched successfully across all nodes; data parallelism and gradient accumulation active; training loop executing with automatic device coordination.

Configure Accelerate with your hardware setup, then use its launcher to start training. The skill handles coordination across devices automatically.

skill_drafts.name: SLURM Multi-Node Training Job Configuration
skill_drafts.description: Define and submit SLURM job scripts to coordinate training across multiple compute nodes with dedicated generation nodes, specifying resource allocation, node assignment, and inter-node communication.
skill_drafts.objective: Configure and submit scalable multi-node training jobs on HPC clusters
applicable_signals: Allocating multiple nodes for large model training
Separating training and generation workloads across nodes
Training models larger than single-node GPU memory capacity
contraindications: Cloud-managed training platforms without SLURM access
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Define SLURM header directives', 'detail': 'Specify job name, partition, number of nodes, tasks per node, GPUs per node, time limit, and output/error log paths'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Allocate training nodes', 'detail': 'Reserve N nodes for distributed training with DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3 and Accelerate configuration'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Allocate generation nodes', 'detail': 'Reserve dedicated node(s) for vLLM-powered generation, separate from training node pool'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Configure inter-node communication', 'detail': 'Set environment variables for distributed training (MASTER_ADDR, MASTER_PORT, RANK, WORLD_SIZE)'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Load required modules and activate environment', 'detail': 'Load CUDA, cuDNN, and other dependencies; activate Python virtual environment'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Launch training on training nodes', 'detail': 'Use srun or torchrun to start training script on allocated training nodes'}
{'step': 7, 'action': 'Launch generation service on generation nodes', 'detail': 'Start vLLM server on dedicated generation node(s) in parallel with training'}
{'step': 8, 'action': 'Submit job to SLURM queue', 'detail': 'Execute sbatch command with configured script; verify job submission and obtain job ID'}
triggers: Submitting jobs to SLURM-managed clusters; allocating multiple nodes for training; separating training and generation workloads across nodes
constraints: SLURM cluster must be available and accessible
Sufficient GPU nodes must be available in the partition
Training and generation nodes must have compatible GPU types
Network connectivity between nodes must be stable
DeepSpeed and Accelerate must be installed in the environment
vLLM must be installed on generation nodes
cautions: Ensure MASTER_ADDR and MASTER_PORT are correctly set to avoid communication failures
Verify node count and GPU allocation match model size requirements
Monitor job logs for inter-node communication errors
Set appropriate time limits to avoid premature job termination
Confirm generation node is reachable from training nodes before job starts
output_contract: SLURM job script created and validated; job successfully submitted to queue; training nodes allocated and confirmed; generation nodes reserved and isolated; job status visible in squeue output; inter-node communication established and verified

examples.input: Train Qwen2.5-72B model on 4 training nodes with 1 dedicated generation node
examples.output: SLURM script with #SBATCH directives for 5 total nodes, 4 assigned to training with DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3, 1 assigned to vLLM generation; job submitted with sbatch; job ID returned
examples.notes: Example from source: training on 4 nodes, generation on 5th node
